acceptanceCriteria: When `corvint context` (and other snapshot readers) runs without a usable snapshot, its output names that it did a full build and how long it took, and suggests `corvint index`; read-only behaviour is unchanged.
The lane charter / DOGFOOD.md pre-change step runs `corvint index` once per fresh checkout before context or impact reads.
sourceImports skips files that cannot contain an import before running the regex, with byte-identical index output (test retained) and the measured build-time change recorded.
body: Evidence: owner-requested performance search on 2026-10-17. Measured with corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 build 615, corvint-tasks build 615, Go 1.27.2, macOS 12-core/64 GB host at load average 80-84 (wall times are inflated by load; CPU times are the stable signal). Lane counts come from orchestrator session 03e2afac subagent transcripts (206 lanes). `corvint context` reads a snapshot only when `corvint index` wrote one and never writes one itself (cmd/corvint/taskcontext.go). In a fresh clone or worktree every call does a full in-memory build: measured 22.76 s wall, 7.25 s user, 813-840 MB max RSS at origin/main c92ee0015 with no snapshot, versus 5.82 s wall, 0.43 s user in the primary checkout with a snapshot of its tree. Lane transcripts show 46 `corvint context` calls but only 6 `corvint index` calls, so most lane context calls paid the full build (transcript p50 16.0 s). CPU profile of the no-snapshot call: compileSources 30%, tokeniseSource/buildTermTable 15%, sourceImports regexp.FindAllStringSubmatchIndex 14.5% (an import regex run over every source; a cheap byte prefilter could skip most files), buildSymbolWindows 12%, worktreePin 10%. Snapshots are now 138-163 MB per tree with a recorded 37.8 s build (V1-0328 still says 63 MB). Related: V1-0418 (dirty-worktree overlay).

title: corvint context rebuilds the whole index on every call in a checkout without a snapshot: 22.8 s and 813 MB versus 5.8 s
